p: the city sit desolate: The prophet wonders at the great judgment of God, seeing Jerusalem, which was so strong and so full of people, to be now destroyed and desolate.
and princess among the provinces: Who had chief rule over many provinces and countries.
night: So that she takes no rest.
lovers she hath none to comfort: Meaning the Egyptians and Assyrians who promised help.
of affliction: For her cruelty toward the poor and oppression of servants, Jer 34:11.
to the solemn feasts: As they used to come up with mirth and joy, Ps 42:4.
are the head: That is, have rule over her, De 28:41.
like harts that find no pasture: As men pined away with sorrow and that have no courage.
fell into the hand of the: In her misery she considered the great benefits and commodities that she had lost.
sabbaths: At her religion and serving of God, which was the greatest grief to the godly.
Her filthiness is in her skirts: She is not ashamed of her sin, although it is revealed.
thou didst command that they should: God forbids the Ammonites and Moabites to enter into the congregation of the Lord, and under them he comprehends all enemies, De 23:3.
sorrow like my sorrow: Thus Jerusalem laments moving others to pity her and to learn by her example.
he sent fire into my bones: This declares that we should acknowledge God to be the author of all our afflictions to the intent that we might seek him for remedy.
yoke of my transgressions is bound: My heavy sins are continually before his eyes as he that ties a thing to his hand for a reminder.
winepress: He has trodden them underfoot as they tread grapes in the winepress.
as a menstruous woman among them: Who because of her pollution was separate from her husband, Le 15:19 and was abhorred for the time.
sought their food to relieve their: That is, they died for hunger.
Let all their wickedness come before: Of desiring vengeance against the enemy, See Geneva "Jer 11:20" and See Geneva "Jer 18:21"
